items.title: A convex mixture of probability laws is a probability law
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space, let $P,Q$ be probability measures on it, and let $t\in[0,1]$. The set function $M_t(A)=(1-t)P(A)+tQ(A)$ is a probability measure.

items.title: A common data law forces a two-point tail-loss bound
items.statement: Let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal G,R)$ be a probability space and let $\Theta$ be a measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) with $\theta_0,\theta_1\in\Theta$. Let $\hat\theta:\mathcal Z\to\Theta$ be measurable and let $\ell:\Theta\times\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$ have measurable sections $a\mapsto\ell(\theta_i,a)$. If $\max\{\ell(\theta_0,a),\ell(\theta_1,a)\}\ge\kappa\ell(\theta_0,\theta_1)$ for every $a\in\Theta$, where $\kappa>0$, then $\max_{i=0,1}R\{\ell(\theta_i,\hat\theta)\ge\kappa\ell(\theta_0,\theta_1)\}\ge1/2$.

items.title: Gross-error contamination path
items.statement: For probability measures $F,H$ on a common measurable space $(X,\mathcal A)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]) and $0\le\epsilon\le1$, the gross-error path is $F_{\epsilon,H}=(1-\epsilon)F+\epsilon H$, a probability measure by [[lem-convex-mixture-of-probability-laws]]. For any $x\in X$, its point-contamination direction at $x$ is the specialization $H=\delta_x$ ([[def-dirac-measure]], [[prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure]]). The path is used for a derivative at $\epsilon=0$; the definition alone gives no uniform-in-$H$ remainder.

items.title: The mean has an unbounded directional derivative supremum
items.statement: On $\mathbb R$ with its Borel sigma-algebra, for $F=\delta_0$ and $H=\delta_a$, the mean functional $T(G)=\int x\,dG(x)$ has $T(F_{\epsilon,H})=\epsilon a$ and right derivative $a$ at $\epsilon=0$. Each path law has finite support and hence a finite first moment. Taking the supremum of the absolute derivatives over $a\in\mathbb R$ gives $+\infty$.
